To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the HPA axis is reset to a higher level in systemic disease, the GH axis is reset to an elevated level, the TSH and PRL axes are reset to a decreased level, and the reproductive axis is impaired
the hypothalamic pituitary axis is altered in a variety of ways in a variety of systemic illnesses.
'In systemic disease, the hypothalamic and pituitary hormones are altered in a manner that is teleologically favourable to survival'.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the elucidation of the mechanisms involved in the regulation of the neuroendocrine system.
the elucidation of the neuroendocrine mechanisms involved in the control of the HPA, GH, TSH, PRL, gonadal and adrenal axes.
the study of the neuroendocrine control of the hypothalamic-hypophyseal-adrenal axis and the pituitary-thyroid axis in health and disease.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the hypothalamic and pituitary changes in systemic disease are complex, and are not well understood at this time.
the hypothalamic and pituitary responses to systemic illness are complex and variable.
the hypothalamus-pituitary axis is a complex and highly adaptive system which is capable of responding to a wide range of physiological stimuli and stressors.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the pituitary is a dynamic organ that responds to the needs of the organism.
the pituitary gland is a highly adaptable and plastic structure that can be modified in response to a number of different stimuli.

the hypothalamo-pituitary system is a highly sensitive and adaptable system that responds to changes in the body's needs and in the external environment in a manner that is favourable to the survival of the organism.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the pituitary gland is a very sensitive barometer of the state of the body and that the pituitaries of many patients with systemic disease have a very different profile of hormone secretion than normal controls.
the hypothalamus and pituitary gland are not isolated from systemic influences and, in fact, respond to them in a manner that may be adaptive to the organism.
the pituitary gland is a dynamic organ that responds to the needs of the body in a variety of circumstances.
